newsitem.title: POLAND: Floods kill 39 in Poland, Czech Republic.
newsitem.headline: Floods kill 39 in Poland, Czech Republic.

text.p: Republic unleashed by days of torrential rain have killed at least 39 people and forced tens of thousands to flee their homes, civil defence officials said on Thursday.

In Poland, civil defence spokesman Captain Leszek Korpus said 20,000 had been evacuated and more would have to leave as flood tides on the Oder river hit the southwestern city Opole, swamping its old town and cutting off the left bank part.

Lieutenant Jacek Podgorski, spokesman for the government's flood-crisis committee, said Poland's confirmed death toll had risen to 22 but could grow further because communications with flooded zones had collapsed at midday.
The Polish telecommunications monopoly TPSA said 42,000 phones were out of order in three inundated provinces.
Deaths were reported in Walbrzych province, Bielsko-Biala region, Opole, Nowy Sacz, Katowice, Jelenia Gora and Legnica.
Korpus said 310,000 hectares (682 acres) of land were under water, including 10 towns and seven villages.
The situation was improving in the Legnica and Jelenia Gora regions but deteriorating along the Oder valley, threatening the major industrial cities of Katowice and Wroclaw.
Korpus said more than 15,000 firefighters, soldiers, border guards and policemen were involved in rescue efforts.
There were no damage estimates yet.
Flooding in the neighbouring Czech Republic, the worst this century, moved downstream on the Morava and Opava rivers to the southeast while easing in the stricken north, officials said.

Scores of soldiers, firemen and rescuers continued to evacuate thousands of people from downstream towns and villages in a disaster that had killed at least 17 people, the local news agency CTK said. Dozens of people were missing.
Houses were swept away as flood waters inundated the large cities of Ostrava, on the border with Poland, and Olomouc.
Flooding also affected nearby Slovakia and Austria.
Heavy rains swelled several Slovak rivers and streams to 100-year record levels, mainly in the northwest of the country. But damage was said to be limited without loss of life.
Slovak troops had to evacuate 15,000 inhabitants from the western spa town of Piestany on the Vah River, Slovakia's longest, the official news agency TASR said on Thursday.
